newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics declines comment on rumors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics declines comment on rumors.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp declined to comment on whether it is close to shipping a new modem.
Shares of U.S. Robotics were up 4-3/8 on continued speculation that the company will market a faster modem by the end of the year, securities analysts said.
"We haven't even confirmed the rumors," said Kitty Behof, a spokeswoman for U.S. Robotics. "The company is saying 33.6 is not the end of line and we are working to develop faster speeds."
A faster modem would spark more sales of the on-line service hubs to which users connect, analysts said. To get a faster connection, both sides of the equation would have to be upgraded.
U.S. Robotics has a dominant market share for both the modems and hubs, analysts said.
"They see these faster modems, people will buy more of these hubs, so that will also drive the sales of the total control hubs," said Volpe, Welty & Co analyst Amar Senan.

Earlier this week, Rockwell International Corp's semiconductor group said it expects to demonstrate 56 kilobits per second transmission capabilities at a trade show in November. Analysts said they expect U.S. Robotics to be able to ship a quicker modem first.
A 33.6 kilobits per second modem is available, but a 28.8 modem is typically used by Internet surfers and online services.
"What they will do is instead of sitting around and getting frustrated with 28.8 they will upgrade," said Steven Levy, an analyst for Oppenheimer & Co.
Earlier this week U.S. Robotics stock hit 66-1/2, its highest level in a month. The last time the stock closed lower was last Thursday.
